o1.biggest_strength: Exceptional business acumen, from recognizing that free accounts cost $0 in cash to identifying the cannibalization risk of extending the credit window.
o1.biggest_mistake: Proposing a mixed commission rate (40% then 30%) might require extra tech work to configure in standard affiliate tools, though it brilliantly neutralizes the rival.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: It is already a 10. The phrase 'Finance is right to protect margin. It just isn't in the rate' is brilliant.

o2.biggest_strength: Very clear, direct communication and excellent tabular formatting that makes the first 30 days plan instantly actionable.
o2.biggest_mistake: Deducting $12,480 for free software plans from a hard $40,000 cash budget, which misunderstands the zero marginal cost of SaaS.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Recognizing that software accounts don't consume the cash budget, freeing up that $12,480 for real cash perks.

reason: Both did a phenomenal job and nailed the lifetime value math, but candidate 1 understood SaaS economics better (free accounts don't use up cash budget) and foresaw the risk of paying more for sales we already get.
